subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should incremental session-memory indexing be pursued as a fresh current-main implementation, as a rescue of the open candidate PR, or intentionally left as full-entry reindex behavior with existing delta/cache controls?
rationale: The choice affects session-state correctness, memory_index schema behavior, source-wide batching, overlap semantics, and whether the existing conflicting candidate branch is worth adopting.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index_* schema and batching paths with upgrade, compaction, and real-behavior proof.

options.title: Rescue the open candidate PR
options.body: Ask for a rebase and replacement of obsolete assumptions in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 before further review.

options.title: Keep full-entry reindexing
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide consistency and simplicity are preferable to incremental session indexing complexity.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index_* schema and batching paths with upgrade, compaction, and real-behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session transcript corpus and identity work makes this the strongest available owner for the design choice.
